subcategories.label: Painting
subcategories.definition: Paintings, painters, genres, and painting methods across periods; use a period tag as well when useful.

subcategories.label: Sculpture and Installation Art
subcategories.definition: Sculptures, sculptors, monuments as artworks, and spatial or installation-based art.

subcategories.label: Drawing, Prints, and Illustration
subcategories.definition: Drawing, engraving, woodcuts, lithography, illustrated images, and their makers and techniques.

subcategories.label: Photography, Film, and Digital Art
subcategories.definition: Photography and time-based or digital works studied as fine art, including experimental film.

subcategories.label: Architecture and Urban Design
subcategories.definition: Buildings, architects, architectural styles, landscape architecture, and designed urban spaces.

subcategories.label: Decorative Arts, Crafts, and Design
subcategories.definition: Ceramics, textiles, glass, furniture, jewelry, and functional objects studied for artistic design.

subcategories.label: Ancient and Medieval Art
subcategories.definition: Visual art and architecture before the European Renaissance, including ancient civilizations and medieval traditions.

subcategories.label: Renaissance Art
subcategories.definition: European Renaissance and Mannerist visual art and architecture, including Northern and Italian traditions.

subcategories.label: Baroque and Rococo Art
subcategories.definition: Baroque and Rococo visual art and architecture of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

subcategories.label: Neoclassical, Romantic, and Realist Art
subcategories.definition: Visual movements from Neoclassicism through nineteenth-century Romanticism and Realism; excludes musical Romanticism.

subcategories.label: Impressionism and Post-Impressionism
subcategories.definition: Impressionist and Post-Impressionist visual artists, works, and techniques.

subcategories.label: Modern and Contemporary Art
subcategories.definition: Modernist movements and later visual art, including Cubism, Surrealism, abstraction, Pop Art, and conceptual art.

subcategories.label: Art of Asia, Africa, Oceania, and Indigenous Americas
subcategories.definition: Visual traditions of these regions and peoples, including historical and contemporary works; geography alone is insufficient.

subcategories.label: Art Techniques and Interpretation
subcategories.definition: Composition, perspective, color, materials, symbolism, and methods of interpreting or making visual art.

subcategories.label: Museums, Awards, and Arts Institutions
subcategories.definition: Museums, galleries, collections, patrons, exhibitions, artistic awards and honors, and institutions supporting the arts.

subcategories.label: Medieval and Renaissance Music
subcategories.definition: Early European sacred and secular music, including chant, polyphony, and Renaissance composers.

subcategories.label: Baroque Music
subcategories.definition: Baroque composers, works, styles, and practices, including Bach, Handel, and Vivaldi.

subcategories.label: Classical-Period Music
subcategories.definition: Music of the Classical period, including Haydn and Mozart; excludes classical music as an all-period umbrella.

subcategories.label: Romantic Music
subcategories.definition: Nineteenth-century Romantic composers, works, and musical styles; transitional figures may receive adjacent period tags.

subcategories.label: Modern and Contemporary Classical Music
subcategories.definition: Twentieth- and twenty-first-century concert music, including musical Impressionism, modernism, minimalism, and experimental music.

subcategories.label: Orchestral and Band Music
subcategories.definition: Symphonies, concertos, overtures, tone poems, orchestras, wind and military bands, marches, and conductors associated with these ensemble traditions.

subcategories.label: Chamber and Solo Instrumental Music
subcategories.definition: Small-ensemble and solo repertoire, including sonatas, quartets, and piano works; concertos belong under Orchestral Music.

subcategories.label: Opera
subcategories.definition: Operas, composers, singers, librettos, and the conventions of staged opera.

subcategories.label: Choral and Vocal Music
subcategories.definition: Choirs, singing, vocal technique, art songs, masses, oratorios, and other vocal concert or sacred music outside staged opera; ordinary speech and anatomical voice mechanisms belong to other primary categories.

subcategories.label: Jazz and Blues
subcategories.definition: Jazz and blues works, performers, styles, improvisation, and traditions within this primary category.

subcategories.label: Folk and Traditional Music
subcategories.definition: Folk songs, traditional musical practices, and regional or community music traditions worldwide.

subcategories.label: Popular and Screen Music
subcategories.definition: Popular songs and film, television, or game scores whose study topics already belong to Arts and Music.

subcategories.label: Melody, Harmony, and Musical Structure
subcategories.definition: Pitch, scales, keys, chords, notation, counterpoint, and musical forms such as fugue or sonata form.

subcategories.label: Musical Performance and Live Events
subcategories.definition: Live musical performance, concerts, festivals, performance practices, rhythm, meter, tempo, dynamics, articulation, and expressive directions.

subcategories.label: String Instruments
subcategories.definition: Bowed and plucked string instruments, their parts, acoustical features, and playing techniques.

subcategories.label: Wind Instruments
subcategories.definition: Woodwind and brass instruments, their parts, families, and playing techniques.

subcategories.label: Keyboard and Percussion Instruments
subcategories.definition: Pianos, organs, keyboard instruments, pitched and unpitched percussion, and associated playing methods.

subcategories.label: Musical Theater
subcategories.definition: Stage musicals, their songs, creators, performers, and theatrical conventions.

subcategories.label: Ballet and Dance
subcategories.definition: Ballet, modern and traditional dance, choreography, dancers, and dance performance practices.

subcategories.label: Theater and Stagecraft
subcategories.definition: Theatrical performance, acting, directing, stage design, and theater institutions; literary analysis of plays remains in Literature.

subcategories.label: Foods and Ingredients
subcategories.definition: Foods, crops as ingredients, animal products, flavorings, and their everyday culinary uses.

subcategories.label: Cooking and World Cuisines
subcategories.definition: Dishes, cooking methods, regional cuisines, culinary customs, cooks, and cookbooks.

subcategories.label: Drinks and Drinking Culture
subcategories.definition: Tea, coffee, soft drinks, alcoholic beverages, preparation, and social drinking traditions.

subcategories.label: Clothing, Textiles, and Fashion
subcategories.definition: Garments, textiles, jewelry, fashion movements, and traditions of dress and personal presentation.

subcategories.label: Holidays, Celebrations, and Life Customs
subcategories.definition: Festivals, weddings, funerals, calendars in daily life, etiquette, naming customs, and rites of passage.

subcategories.label: Family, Communities, and Social Traditions
subcategories.definition: Families, childhood, social relationships, interpersonal practices and gestures, cultural communities, identities, national symbols, flags, color meanings, folklore in daily culture, and social traditions.

subcategories.label: Homes, Materials, and Everyday Objects
subcategories.definition: Household goods, tools, defensive objects, building materials, crafts, furnishings, appliances, ordinary manufactured objects, and practical natural materials including nonfood plant fibers and products.

subcategories.label: Transportation and Travel
subcategories.definition: Vehicles, transportation services, travel customs, tourism, accommodation, and everyday mobility.

subcategories.label: Businesses, Shopping, and Consumer Culture
subcategories.definition: Brands, retailers, consumer services, advertising, money in daily use, and shopping practices.

subcategories.label: Work, Education, and Community Services
subcategories.definition: Occupations, schools, libraries, civic services, public facilities and access, community institutions, and everyday working life, including subsistence occupations.

subcategories.label: Recreation, Hobbies, and Outdoor Life
subcategories.definition: Toys, amusement parks, pastimes, camping, hunting, fishing, and noncompetitive leisure activities.

subcategories.label: Communication and Everyday Language
subcategories.definition: Everyday language, writing conventions, symbols, communication media, and the practical exchange of information.

subcategories.label: Health, Grooming, and Daily Habits
subcategories.definition: Personal care, hairstyles, cosmetics, sanitation, everyday health and substance-use practices, and habits such as smoking; classify cultural and practical aspects rather than biological mechanisms.

subcategories.label: United States and Canada
subcategories.definition: Places and geographic features in the United States and Canada, including states, provinces, and territories.

subcategories.label: Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean
subcategories.definition: Places and geographic features in Mexico, Central America, and Caribbean countries and territories.

subcategories.label: South America
subcategories.definition: Places and geographic features in South America and its associated islands.

subcategories.label: British Isles
subcategories.definition: Geography of Great Britain, Ireland, and surrounding islands; the label does not imply political unity.

subcategories.label: Western and Northern Europe
subcategories.definition: Continental Western Europe and the Nordic countries; excludes the British Isles and places better classified in other European regions.

subcategories.label: Southern Europe
subcategories.definition: Iberia, Italy, Greece, and the southern Balkans; use Eastern Europe as well only for substantial regional overlap.

subcategories.label: Central and Eastern Europe
subcategories.definition: Central Europe, eastern European countries, and the inland Balkans; Russian geography has a separate regional tag.

subcategories.label: Russia and Central Asia
subcategories.definition: Russia, including Siberia, and the Central Asian republics; excludes the South Caucasus.

subcategories.label: Middle East and North Africa
subcategories.definition: North Africa, Southwest Asia, Turkey, Iran, and the South Caucasus as geographic regions.

subcategories.label: Sub-Saharan Africa
subcategories.definition: West, Central, East, and Southern Africa, including Madagascar and nearby islands.

subcategories.label: South Asia
subcategories.definition: The Indian subcontinent, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Afghanistan, and associated physical regions.

subcategories.label: East Asia
subcategories.definition: China, Japan, the Korean Peninsula, Mongolia, Taiwan, and associated physical regions.

subcategories.label: Southeast Asia
subcategories.definition: Mainland and maritime Southeast Asia, including Indonesia and the Philippines.

subcategories.label: Australia, New Zealand, and Pacific Islands
subcategories.definition: Australia, New Zealand, Melanesia, Micronesia, Polynesia, and their physical geography.

subcategories.label: Polar Regions
subcategories.definition: The Arctic, Antarctica, polar islands, and geographic features defined by their polar setting.

subcategories.label: Countries, Territories, and Borders
subcategories.definition: Sovereign states, dependencies, disputed territories, borders, and political divisions. A physical island or region is not a political entity merely because it contains countries; use this tag only when political status or division defines the topic.

subcategories.label: States, Provinces, and Regions
subcategories.definition: Subnational administrative divisions and named cultural or geographic regions, including U.S. states and ecclesiastical districts considered as territorial units.

subcategories.label: Cities, Capitals, and Settlements
subcategories.definition: Cities, capitals, towns, metropolitan areas, and settlement locations or characteristics.

subcategories.label: Mountains, Volcanoes, and Uplands
subcategories.definition: Mountains, mountain ranges, volcanoes, plateaus, and upland regions as geographic features.

subcategories.label: Rivers and Drainage Basins
subcategories.definition: Rivers, tributaries, watersheds, river systems, waterfalls, and their geographic relationships.

subcategories.label: Lakes, Groundwater, and Inland Waters
subcategories.definition: Lakes, reservoirs, inland seas, aquifers, groundwater systems, and other land-enclosed or subsurface bodies of water.

subcategories.label: Oceans, Seas, and Coasts
subcategories.definition: Oceans, marginal seas, gulfs, bays, straits, shorelines, and coastal geography.

subcategories.label: Islands and Archipelagos
subcategories.definition: Islands and island groups, including their locations, formation as landforms, and geographic relationships.

subcategories.label: Deserts, Plains, and Other Landforms
subcategories.definition: Deserts, plains, valleys, canyons, caves, peninsulas, and landforms outside the other physical-feature groups.

subcategories.label: Climate, Biomes, and Natural Landscapes
subcategories.definition: Climate regions, forests, grasslands, wetlands, and large-scale environmental patterns in a geographic context.

subcategories.label: Parks, Reserves, and Natural Heritage
subcategories.definition: National parks, protected areas, wildlife reserves, and natural heritage sites.

subcategories.label: Landmarks, Buildings, and Historic Sites
subcategories.definition: Built landmarks, monuments, archaeological sites, and notable buildings considered as places. A city does not qualify merely because clues mention buildings within it.

subcategories.label: Transportation Routes and Infrastructure
subcategories.definition: Canals, roads, railways, ports, airports, bridges, and geographic transport networks.

subcategories.label: Population, Culture, and Economic Geography
subcategories.definition: Migration, population distribution, urbanization, cultural landscapes, resources, and economic activity organized by place.

subcategories.label: Maps, Navigation, and Geographic Concepts
subcategories.definition: Maps, coordinates, cartography, time zones, navigation, geographic measurement, and general geographic terminology.

subcategories.label: British Literature
subcategories.definition: Literature associated with England, Scotland, Wales, and British literary traditions; use Irish Literature for distinct Irish traditions.

subcategories.label: U.S. and Canadian Literature
subcategories.definition: Literature of the United States and Canada, including their regional, Indigenous, and diasporic literary traditions.

subcategories.label: Irish Literature
subcategories.definition: Irish authors, works, and literary traditions, including Irish-language and English-language writing.

subcategories.label: French Literature
subcategories.definition: French and Francophone literary traditions; also use African or Caribbean traditions when those contexts are central.

subcategories.label: German-Language Literature
subcategories.definition: German-language literature from Germany, Austria, Switzerland, and other associated traditions.

subcategories.label: Russian and Eastern European Literature
subcategories.definition: Russian, Slavic, and other Eastern European literary traditions, including their writers and works.

subcategories.label: Southern European Literature
subcategories.definition: Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Greek, and related Southern European traditions after classical antiquity.

subcategories.label: Northern European Literature
subcategories.definition: Scandinavian, Icelandic, Finnish, Dutch, and other Northern European traditions outside British and German-language literature.

subcategories.label: Latin American and Caribbean Literature
subcategories.definition: Literature of Latin America and the Caribbean, including regional movements and diasporic traditions.

subcategories.label: African Literature
subcategories.definition: African literary traditions across languages, regions, and periods, including African diasporic contexts when central.

subcategories.label: Middle Eastern Literature
subcategories.definition: Arabic, Persian, Turkish, Hebrew, and other Middle Eastern literary traditions.

subcategories.label: South Asian Literature
subcategories.definition: Literature of the Indian subcontinent and its diasporas across languages and periods.

subcategories.label: East and Southeast Asian Literature
subcategories.definition: Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, and other East or Southeast Asian literary traditions.

subcategories.label: Indigenous and Oceanian Literature
subcategories.definition: Indigenous literary traditions and the literature of Australia, New Zealand, and Pacific communities.

subcategories.label: Ancient Greek and Roman Literature
subcategories.definition: Classical Greek and Latin authors, works, genres, and literary traditions.

subcategories.label: Medieval Literature
subcategories.definition: Medieval literary works and traditions, including courtly romance and medieval epics; use regional dates when appropriate.

subcategories.label: Renaissance and Early Modern Literature
subcategories.definition: Renaissance and early modern literature through the seventeenth century, including Elizabethan and Jacobean drama.

subcategories.label: Enlightenment and Eighteenth-Century Literature
subcategories.definition: Eighteenth-century and Enlightenment writing, including neoclassicism and the development of the modern novel.

subcategories.label: Romanticism, Symbolism, and Decadence
subcategories.definition: Literary Romanticism, Symbolism, and Decadence, including their major authors, works, and ideas; a broad movement grouping, not a claim that the movements are identical. Excludes romance as a plot genre.

subcategories.label: Realism, Naturalism, and Victorian Literature
subcategories.definition: Victorian writing, literary realism, naturalism, social realism, and associated protest literature across periods, including characteristic authors, works, and movements.

subcategories.label: Modernist Literature
subcategories.definition: Literary modernism, its major writers and works, and associated experimentation in form and perspective.

subcategories.label: Postwar and Contemporary Literature
subcategories.definition: Literature from approximately 1945 onward, including postmodernism and current writing; avoid tagging earlier careers solely by death date.

subcategories.label: Novels and Novellas
subcategories.definition: Long-form narrative fiction, novels and novellas, including verse novels and graphic novels, and writers substantially associated with these forms. Also assign Poetry or visual-narrative forms when central.

subcategories.label: Short Stories
subcategories.definition: Short fiction, story collections, short-story writers, and conventions specific to the form.

subcategories.label: Poetry
subcategories.definition: Poems, poets, poetic forms, and verse traditions, including narrative and lyric poetry.

subcategories.label: Drama
subcategories.definition: Plays, playwrights, and literary dramatic forms, including tragedy and comedy; stagecraft belongs in Arts and Music.

subcategories.label: Essays, Memoirs, and Literary Nonfiction
subcategories.definition: Essays, autobiography, biography, travel writing, and nonfiction studied for literary significance.

subcategories.label: Children's and Young Adult Literature
subcategories.definition: Works, writers, and traditions intended substantially for children or adolescent readers.

subcategories.label: Science Fiction and Fantasy
subcategories.definition: Speculative fiction, imagined worlds, speculative technologies, and fantasy traditions in literature.

subcategories.label: Gothic and Horror Literature
subcategories.definition: Gothic fiction, supernatural terror, horror writing, and their characteristic authors, works, and conventions.

subcategories.label: Mystery, Crime, and Adventure Fiction
subcategories.definition: Detective stories, thrillers, crime fiction, and adventure-centered literature.

subcategories.label: Historical and War Literature
subcategories.definition: Historical fiction and literature centrally concerned with war or its aftermath; excludes works merely written during wartime.

subcategories.label: Satire and Humor
subcategories.definition: Literary satire, parody, comic writing, and works using humor as a central artistic method.

subcategories.label: Folktales, Fables, and Oral Traditions
subcategories.definition: Fairy tales, folktales, fables, oral storytelling, and their literary retellings.

subcategories.label: Literary Forms, Visual Narrative, and Criticism
subcategories.definition: Narrative devices, rhetoric, prosody, literary terminology, graphic novels and comics as visual narrative, and critical approaches or theories. Provides a literary route for sequential art as well as literary techniques.

subcategories.label: Literature of Race, Gender, and Colonialism
subcategories.definition: Literary traditions and works centrally engaging racial identity, gender, colonialism, or postcolonial experience.

subcategories.label: Religious and Philosophical Literature
subcategories.definition: Works studied as literature whose central structures or concerns are religious, spiritual, or philosophical.

subcategories.label: Literary Institutions and Book Culture
subcategories.definition: Publishing, literary prizes, book history, reference works, dictionaries and lexicography, libraries as literary institutions, and organized literary communities.

subcategories.label: Numbers, Arithmetic, and Measurement
subcategories.definition: Number systems, arithmetic operations, fractions, ratios, elementary measurement, and named individual numbers.

subcategories.label: Number Theory
subcategories.definition: Primes, divisibility, integer properties, modular arithmetic, and equations studied for integer solutions.

subcategories.label: Algebra and Equations
subcategories.definition: Expressions, polynomials, equations, inequalities, and algebraic manipulation outside specialized linear or abstract algebra.

subcategories.label: Functions, Sequences, and Series
subcategories.definition: Functions and their properties, sequences, summation, recurrence, and finite or infinite series.

subcategories.label: Plane Geometry
subcategories.definition: Lines, angles, triangles, polygons, circles, congruence, and measurement in two-dimensional geometry.

subcategories.label: Solid Geometry
subcategories.definition: Three-dimensional shapes, polyhedra, spheres, volumes, surface areas, and spatial geometric relationships.

subcategories.label: Coordinate Geometry
subcategories.definition: Cartesian and polar coordinates, geometric graphs, slopes, conic sections, and algebraic descriptions of shapes.

subcategories.label: Trigonometry
subcategories.definition: Trigonometric functions, identities, triangle relations, and angle-based calculation.

subcategories.label: Calculus and Differential Equations
subcategories.definition: Limits, derivatives, integrals, differential equations, and applications of calculus.

subcategories.label: Mathematical Analysis
subcategories.definition: Continuity, convergence, real and complex analysis, and rigorous properties of mathematical functions and spaces.

subcategories.label: Linear Algebra
subcategories.definition: Vectors, matrices, determinants, linear transformations, and systems of linear equations.

subcategories.label: Abstract Algebra
subcategories.definition: Groups, rings, fields, algebraic structures, and their structural relationships.

subcategories.label: Probability
subcategories.definition: Random events, conditional probability, expected values, and probability distributions.

subcategories.label: Statistics
subcategories.definition: Data summaries, sampling, statistical inference, hypothesis tests, regression, and interpreting variation.

subcategories.label: Combinatorics and Graph Theory
subcategories.definition: Counting, arrangements, permutations, combinations, graphs, networks, and discrete configurations.

subcategories.label: Logic, Sets, Notation, and Proof
subcategories.definition: Logical operations, set theory, infinity, mathematical notation and symbols, formal foundations, and methods or limits of proof. Includes notation such as summation and product signs.

subcategories.label: Topology and Advanced Geometry
subcategories.definition: Topology, non-Euclidean and differential geometry, fractals, and geometric properties beyond elementary shape measurement.

subcategories.label: Mathematical History and Applications
subcategories.definition: Mathematicians, historical texts, numerical methods, optimization, modeling, and cross-field applications; people also receive substantive field tags when known.

subcategories.label: Film History, Filmmakers, and Industry
subcategories.definition: Directors, studios, film movements, production, cinematography, editing, visual style, awards, and cinema history spanning genres.

subcategories.label: Film Acting and Screen Personalities
subcategories.definition: Actors, screen performers, and public entertainment careers substantially associated with film.

subcategories.label: Film Drama and Historical Cinema
subcategories.definition: Dramatic, historical, biographical, romance, and war films whose central identity is outside the other film genres.

subcategories.label: Comedy Films
subcategories.definition: Comic films, comedic film traditions, and characters or creators specifically associated with them.

subcategories.label: Action, Adventure, and Crime Films
subcategories.definition: Action films, thrillers, crime cinema, westerns, and adventure films.

subcategories.label: Science Fiction, Fantasy, and Horror Media
subcategories.definition: Speculative, supernatural, and horror films, television, games, worlds, characters, and recurring narrative concepts across entertainment media. Use relevant medium tags too when useful.

subcategories.label: Animation for Film and Television
subcategories.definition: Animated films, cartoons, animated series, studios, and characters across national traditions.

subcategories.label: Stage and Screen Musicals
subcategories.definition: Stage musicals, film musicals, their songs, creators and performers, soundtracks, and music central to theatrical or screen entertainment.

subcategories.label: Television Drama and Comedy
subcategories.definition: Live-action scripted television, sitcoms, dramatic series, and their characters and creators.

subcategories.label: Documentary, Reality, and Variety Media
subcategories.definition: Documentary films and television, docuseries, reality shows, televised competitions, game shows, talk shows, sketch programs, and variety entertainment.

subcategories.label: Children's and Educational Media
subcategories.definition: Entertainment and educational programming chiefly intended for children, including live-action and animated media.

subcategories.label: News, Broadcasting, and Media Institutions
subcategories.definition: Journalists, broadcasters, media outlets, networks, publishing platforms, and news-oriented programming.

subcategories.label: Comics, Graphic Novels, and Superheroes
subcategories.definition: Comic strips, comic books, graphic novels, superhero traditions, and adaptations centered on those traditions.

subcategories.label: Anime and Manga
subcategories.definition: Japanese animation and comics, their creators, characters, genres, and closely associated adaptations.

subcategories.label: Video Games and Interactive Entertainment
subcategories.definition: Games, characters, creators, studios, platforms, mechanics, and interactive entertainment franchises.

subcategories.label: Internet Culture and Online Creators
subcategories.definition: Memes, online personalities, social platforms as cultural phenomena, web entertainment, and online communities.

subcategories.label: Rock, Punk, and Metal
subcategories.definition: Rock and its major branches, including alternative rock, punk, metal, and associated performers and recordings.

subcategories.label: Pop and Dance Music
subcategories.definition: Pop, electronic dance music, dance-oriented recordings, and their performers and production traditions.

subcategories.label: Hip-Hop and Rap
subcategories.definition: Hip-hop performers, recordings, rap styles, and associated musical culture.

subcategories.label: Soul, R&B, Funk, and Gospel
subcategories.definition: Popular soul, rhythm and blues, funk, gospel, and related performers and recordings.

subcategories.label: Country, Folk, and Singer-Songwriters
subcategories.definition: Country, folk-pop, and acoustic singer-songwriter musical traditions, with their performers and recordings. Writing songs does not by itself place pop, rock, or rap performers in this genre collection.

subcategories.label: Jazz, Blues, and Global Popular Traditions
subcategories.definition: Jazz, blues, reggae, and regional popular traditions such as Latin popular music within this primary category.

subcategories.label: Music Industry, Recording, and Performance
subcategories.definition: Albums as a format, recording, concerts, awards, music distribution, and careers spanning musical genres.

subcategories.label: Live Entertainment and Attractions
subcategories.definition: Stand-up, improvisation, magic, circus, live variety entertainment, theme parks, themed attractions, entertainment resorts, and cross-media entertainment festivals or conferences.

subcategories.label: Greek Gods and Religious Traditions
subcategories.definition: Greek deities, cults, sacred places, religious practices, and divine myths; human heroic narratives have a separate tag.

subcategories.label: Greek Heroes and Mythic Narratives
subcategories.definition: Greek heroes, legendary expeditions, mortal figures, monsters in heroic stories, and major myth cycles.

subcategories.label: Roman Religion and Mythology
subcategories.definition: Roman deities, religious practices, foundation legends, and distinctly Roman mythic traditions.

subcategories.label: Egyptian Religion and Mythology
subcategories.definition: Ancient Egyptian gods, myths, funerary beliefs, texts, and religious practices.

subcategories.label: Mesopotamian and Ancient Near Eastern Traditions
subcategories.definition: Mesopotamian, Canaanite, Phoenician, and related ancient traditions outside biblical and Egyptian categories.

subcategories.label: Norse and Germanic Mythology
subcategories.definition: Norse and other Germanic gods, heroic stories, cosmology, texts, and religious traditions.

subcategories.label: Celtic Traditions and World Folklore
subcategories.definition: Celtic and Slavic religious traditions plus folktales, legends, supernatural beliefs, and oral-story traditions worldwide, including non-European tales. Prefer a specific religious-tradition tag when the topic is primarily that religion.

subcategories.label: Indigenous Traditions of the Americas
subcategories.definition: Religious and mythic traditions of Indigenous peoples of North, Central, and South America.

subcategories.label: African and African Diasporic Traditions
subcategories.definition: African traditional religions and diasporic traditions such as Vodou, including their distinct beliefs and practices.

subcategories.label: Oceanian and Australian Indigenous Traditions
subcategories.definition: Religious and mythic traditions of Pacific peoples and Indigenous Australians.

subcategories.label: Chinese Religions and Mythology
subcategories.definition: Chinese folk religion, Daoism, religious Confucian traditions, deities, myths, and practices.

subcategories.label: Japanese and Korean Religions and Mythology
subcategories.definition: Shinto and other Japanese or Korean religious and mythic traditions; Buddhism may also receive its own tag.

subcategories.label: Hinduism
subcategories.definition: Hindu deities, epics, philosophies in religious context, sacred texts, rituals, and religious communities.

subcategories.label: Buddhism
subcategories.definition: Buddhist teachings, figures, texts, schools, religious practices, and sacred places.

subcategories.label: Sikh, Jain, and Other South Asian and Himalayan Traditions
subcategories.definition: Sikh and Jain beliefs, figures, texts, and practices, plus other South Asian and Himalayan traditions outside the dedicated Hinduism and Buddhism collections, including the distinct Tibetan Bön tradition.

subcategories.label: Zoroastrianism and Other West Asian Traditions
subcategories.definition: Zoroastrian and Iranian religious traditions, plus other West Asian traditions not covered by the Jewish, Christian, or Islamic collections, including Yazidism. This is a regional study grouping, not a claim that these religions are equivalent.

subcategories.label: Hebrew Bible and Biblical Traditions
subcategories.definition: People, narratives, and books of the Hebrew Bible or Christian Old Testament, with tradition-specific interpretations kept distinct.

subcategories.label: Jewish Beliefs, Practices, and History
subcategories.definition: Judaism, rabbinic traditions, Jewish holidays, ritual, religious communities, and religious history beyond biblical narrative alone.

subcategories.label: New Testament and Early Christianity
subcategories.definition: New Testament books, figures, narratives, and the formative history and practices of Christianity.

subcategories.label: Christian Theology and Worship
subcategories.definition: Christian doctrines, sacraments, worship, saints, symbols, and theological concepts across denominations.

subcategories.label: Christian Churches and Religious History
subcategories.definition: Catholic, Orthodox, Protestant, and other Christian communities, institutions, movements, and denominational histories.

subcategories.label: Islamic Beliefs, Texts, and Practices
subcategories.definition: The Quran, Islamic teachings, worship, observances, sacred places, and religious concepts.

subcategories.label: Islamic Figures, Communities, and History
subcategories.definition: Muhammad, other Islamic religious figures, Sunni and Shia traditions, religious movements, and institutions.

subcategories.label: New and Modern Religious Movements
subcategories.definition: Modern religious movements and communities, including modern syncretic movements. Do not use this as a fallback for a longstanding tradition simply because it lacks another obvious label.

subcategories.label: Comparative Rituals, Festivals, and Sacred Places
subcategories.definition: Topics explicitly spanning traditions through ritual, sacred spaces, festivals, food rules, or life-cycle observances.

subcategories.label: Creation, Cosmology, and the Afterlife
subcategories.definition: Religious accounts of origins, cosmic order, death, judgment, and afterlife as central study subjects.

subcategories.label: Mythical Creatures, Objects, and Motifs
subcategories.definition: Supernatural creatures, legendary objects, and recurring mythic patterns, especially topics extending beyond a single narrative.

subcategories.label: Religious Ethics, Spirituality, and Belief
subcategories.definition: Cross-tradition religious ethics, spiritual practices, mysticism, belief and nonbelief, and general religious concepts.

subcategories.label: Motion, Forces, and Mechanics
subcategories.definition: Motion, force, energy, momentum, statics, and classical mechanical laws and systems.

subcategories.label: Gravity, Rotation, and Orbits
subcategories.definition: Gravitation, rotational motion, torque, angular momentum, and orbital mechanics.

subcategories.label: Fluids and Pressure
subcategories.definition: Fluid statics and dynamics, buoyancy, pressure, flow, and the mechanics of liquids and gases.

subcategories.label: Heat and Thermodynamics
subcategories.definition: Temperature, heat transfer, thermodynamic laws, entropy, heat engines, and thermal properties.

subcategories.label: Waves, Sound, and Oscillation
subcategories.definition: Wave behavior, oscillators, resonance, acoustics, and sound production or propagation.

subcategories.label: Light and Optics
subcategories.definition: Light, reflection, refraction, lenses, interference, optical instruments, and electromagnetic radiation as an optical phenomenon.

subcategories.label: Electricity and Circuits
subcategories.definition: Electric charge, fields, potential, current, circuit components, and elementary electrical laws.

subcategories.label: Magnetism and Electromagnetism
subcategories.definition: Magnetic fields, induction, electromagnetic forces, and unified electromagnetic theory.

subcategories.label: Atomic and Quantum Physics
subcategories.definition: Atomic structure, quantum states, spectra, quantum mechanics, and microscopic physical phenomena.

subcategories.label: Nuclear and Particle Physics
subcategories.definition: Nuclei, radioactive processes, nuclear reactions, elementary particles, and fundamental interactions.

subcategories.label: Relativity and Spacetime
subcategories.definition: Special and general relativity, spacetime, relativistic effects, and their physical consequences.

subcategories.label: Physical Quantities and Measurement
